name: Amaranth

facts.how: Leaves cooked like spinach; seeds as grain
facts.value: Protein, vitamins A and C, calcium; seeds are a grain

caution: A safe and nutritious green. Harvest from unsprayed ground, and as with spinach, don't rely on it as your only green day after day. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: Also called pigweed: upright, red-rooted, with dense green flower spikes. One of the world's oldest cultivated greens and grains hiding in the garden as a weed.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: Young leaves cook down like a mild spinach; the tiny seeds thresh out by the thousands and cook into a nutty porridge or grind to flour.
